objective: Implement 32-bit ARM Cortex-M sensor interfacing routine 5.
theory: ARM Cortex-M is a 32-bit RISC processor architecture utilizing the Thumb-2 instruction set, Harvard bus structure, and Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller (NVIC).
algorithm: 1. Load base SRAM address 0x20000000 into register R0.
2. Read 32-bit word from memory [R0] into R1.
flowchart: START -> Execute Sensor Interfacing Step 1 -> Process Data -> Verify Flags/Result -> END
assembly_code:
; ARM Cortex-M Assembly - Sensor Interfacing Ex 5
LDR R0, =0x20000000
LDR R1, [R0]
ADD R1, R1, #5
STR R1, [R0, #4]

step_by_step_execution: Step 1: Fetch and decode Sensor Interfacing instruction for ARM Cortex-M (STM32).
Step 2: Read input operands from memory / registers.
Step 3: Execute ALU operation for Sensor Interfacing.
Step 4: Update status flags (Z, CY, S, P).
Step 5: Store final result into memory.

viva_questions.q: What instruction set is used by ARM Cortex-M processors?
viva_questions.a: Thumb-2 instruction set (mix of 16-bit and 32-bit instructions).

viva_questions.q: What is the purpose of the NVIC in ARM Cortex-M?
viva_questions.a: Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller manages hardware interrupts with low latency.
